title: sdk(python): add route tagging support + docstring examples (incl. streaming)
author: Monica Patel
description:
Context: The Console “usage insights” work needs a stable `route` dimension emitted from SDKs/gateways so customers can attribute spend/latency to app endpoints. This PR adds first-class route tagging support to the Python SDK by plumbing a `route` value into outbound requests and documenting usage (including streaming).

What’s in this PR: (1) Adds an optional `route: str | None` parameter to high-level request helpers (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) and to `RequestOptions`. (2) When set, the SDK sends the canonical route identifier via HTTP header `x-redwood-route` (lowercased by httpx on the wire). (3) Ensures the header is applied consistently for non-streaming and streaming requests (SSE) and for both sync + async clients. (4) Adds docstring examples + minimal guidance on naming conventions (avoid user IDs; keep stable; prefer `service.feature.action` style) and points readers to the Console docs.

Notes / decisions: (a) We do not attempt to normalize/validate route strings in the SDK beyond a basic type/length guard; server-side normalization + cardinality guardrails remain the source of truth. (b) For streaming, the header must be set on the initial request; this PR ensures we apply headers before opening the stream context. (c) Backwards compatible: all new params are optional and default to `None`.

API examples:
- Non-streaming: `client.chat.completions.create(model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct", messages=[...], route="billing.invoice_summarize")`
- Streaming: `for event in client.chat.completions.stream(..., route="support.ticket_reply"): ...`
- RequestOptions: `client.embeddings.create(..., request_options=RequestOptions(route="search.embed_query"))`

Testing: Adds unit tests to assert header presence/absence across sync/async + stream/non-stream paths, and a regression test that streaming still functions when custom headers are merged.

Follow-ups: We should mirror the same `route` ergonomics in the Go SDK (separate PR) and confirm the header key matches the API contract used by the gateway path.

notable_diff_snippets: Added optional `route` param to request helpers and applied as `x-redwood-route` header when provided.

review_conversation: Wei Chen (comment): Can we confirm header name matches the cross-SDK contract? I’ve seen `x-redwood-route` in the draft docs, but want to avoid drift.

Monica Patel (reply): Yep—aligned with the current analytics contract + gateway implementation. Also added a short comment in `_base_client.py` referencing the header key as part of usage insights work (ENG-8432).
Nadia Rahman (comment): Please add a guardrail test for “route not set” so we don’t emit empty header values; those can blow up cardinality as `""`/`"unknown"` later.
Monica Patel (reply): Added `None`/empty-string behavior: `None` means omit header; empty/whitespace routes raise `ValueError` early. Tests updated accordingly.
Alex Martinez (comment): Docstring examples look good. Can we include a streaming snippet explicitly? Most customers will copy/paste from there.
Monica Patel (reply): Added a `stream()` example to chat completions docstring + a note that route is attached to the initial stream request.
Alex Martinez (approval): Approved; thanks for covering streaming + async.
release_notes: Python SDK now supports optional route tagging via `route=` (or `RequestOptions(route=...)`) and forwards it as `x-redwood-route` for usage insights; includes docstring examples and streaming compatibility.
